pairs: Attendite ne justitiam vestram faciatis coram hominibus,
“Pay attention, lest you perform your justice before men,
in order to be seen by them;
alioquin mercedem non habebitis apud Patrem vestrum qui in cælis est.
otherwise you shall not have a reward with your Father, who is in heaven.
do not choose to sound a trumpet before you,
as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the towns,
so that they may be honored by men.
nesciat sinistra tua quid faciat dextera tua:
do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
ut sit eleemosyna tua in abscondito,
so that your almsgiving may be in secret,
non eritis sicut hypocritæ qui amant in synagogis
you should not be like the hypocrites,
et in angulis platearum stantes orare,
who love standing in the synagogues and at the corners of the streets to pray,
so that they may be seen by men.
intra in cubiculum tuum, et clauso ostio,
enter into your room, and having shut the door,
pray to your Father in secret,
putant enim quod in multiloquio suo exaudiantur.
For they think that by their excess of words they might be heeded.
do not choose to imitate them.
For your Father knows what your needs may be,
Therefore, you shall pray in this way:
May your name be kept holy.
Panem nostrum supersubstantialem da nobis hodie,
Give us this day our life-sustaining bread.
sicut et nos dimittimus debitoribus nostris.
as we also forgive our debtors.
Et ne nos inducas in tentationem,
And lead us not into temptation.
Si enim dimiseritis hominibus peccata eorum:
For if you will forgive men their sins,
dimittet et vobis Pater vester cælestis delicta vestra.
your heavenly Father also will forgive you your offenses.
But if you will not forgive men,
nec Pater vester dimittet vobis peccata vestra.
neither will your Father forgive you your sins.
do not choose to become gloomy,
so that their fasting may be apparent to men.
that they have received their reward.
so that your fasting will not be apparent to men,
Nolite thesaurizare vobis thesauros in terra:
Do not choose to store up for yourselves treasures on earth:
Thesaurizate autem vobis thesauros in cælo,
Instead, store up for yourselves treasures in heaven:
ubi neque ærugo, neque tinea demolitur,
where neither rust nor moth consumes,
et ubi fures non effodiunt, nec furantur.
and where thieves do not break in and steal.
Lucerna corporis tui est oculus tuus.
The lamp of your body is your eye.
your entire body will be filled with light.
Si autem oculus tuus fuerit nequam,
But if your eye has been corrupted,
your entire body will be darkened.
Si ergo lumen, quod in te est, tenebræ sunt:
If then the light that is in you is darkness,
how great will that darkness be!
No one is able to serve two masters.
For either he will have hatred for the one,
or he will persevere with the one,
Non potestis Deo servire et mammonæ.
You cannot serve God and wealth.
And so I say to you,
ne solliciti sitis animæ vestræ quid manducetis,
do not be anxious about your life, as to what you will eat,
nor about your body, as to what you will wear.
Nonne anima plus est quam esca,
Is not life more than food,
and the body more than clothing?
Consider the birds of the air,
et Pater vester cælestis pascit illa.
and yet your heavenly Father feeds them.
Nonne vos magis pluris estis illis?
Are you not of much greater value than they are?
Quis autem vestrum cogitans potest adjicere ad staturam suam cubitum unum?
And which of you, by thinking, is able to add one cubit to his stature?
Et de vestimento quid solliciti estis?
And as for clothing, why are you anxious?
Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow;
quoniam nec Salomon in omni gloria sua coopertus est sicut unum ex istis.
that not even Solomon, in all his glory, was arrayed like one of these.
So if God so clothes the grass of the field,
and cast into the oven tomorrow,
how much more will he care for you,
Therefore, do not choose to be anxious,
and with what shall we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek all these things.
Scit enim Pater vester, quia his omnibus indigetis.
Yet your Father knows that you need all these things.
seek first the kingdom of God and his justice,
and all these things shall be added to you as well.
Nolite ergo solliciti esse in crastinum.
Therefore, do not be anxious about tomorrow;
Crastinus enim dies sollicitus erit sibi ipsi:
for the future day will be anxious for itself.
Sufficient for the day is its evil.”
